text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The new document submitted by U.N. envoy Diego Cordovez to the two leaders at negotiations in Montreux is looked upon favourably by the Greek Cypriot side.
- State pathologist criticises pharmacists for giving sedatives to people over the counter without prescriptions. Another woman from Limassol committed suicide with an overdose yesterday.
- The U.N. in Cyprus resume negotiations between the military on the two sides for the adoption of measures to reduce tension along the ceasefire line.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash rejects the new U.N. proposals on Cyprus, but plans to stay on.
- Government denies it authorised a Turkish ship to carry out ecological research off Cyprus.
- No progress is seen forthcoming at the Montreux talks. Denktash has rejected a U.N. document containing new proposals on ways to break the Cyprus stalemate.
- Interview: Deputy foreign ministry undersecretary Inal Batu suggests coordinated action between Greece, Cyprus and Turkey for the simultaneous entry into the European Union of Turkey and Cyprus.
- Cyprus marks 23 years from the anniversary of the second phase of the Turkish invasion.
